label: lora_plus_ssm_fixed
description: Same training configuration as V3, but SSM core parameters are saved BEFORE trainer.save_model() to avoid PEFT's inference_mode freeze. This preserves trained SSM values through the merge pipeline. Isolates the contribution of persistent SSM adaptation vs co-training effect.

lora_config.note: Identical target modules to V3. Hybrid-aware LoRA covering attention + Mamba-2 projections.

ssm_config.ssm_persistence_fix: Save ssm_core_params.pt BEFORE trainer.save_model() to capture trained values before PEFT inference_mode discards gradients

merge_pipeline.step_1: LoRA merge: W_merged = W_base + (alpha/r) * B @ A
merge_pipeline.step_2: SSM injection: direct tensor replacement from ssm_core_params.pt into merged model

verification.method: Compare ssm_core_params.pt A_log values against base model A_log values
verification.result: All 3 tasks show Changed: YES with 108 SSM keys each

key_findings.classification_gain: +3.6 points exact_match over V3 (55.8 vs 52.2), +15.0 total over V2 (55.8 vs 40.8). Decomposition of V2→V4 gain: ~76% from co-training effect (V2→V3: +11.4), ~24% from SSM persistence (V3→V4: +3.6).
key_findings.mapping_neutral: 96.73% vs 96.03% — within noise. Schema mapping task does not benefit significantly from persistent SSM adaptation.
key_findings.code_gen_neutral: 98.8% vs 98.58% — flat. Structured code generation already saturated by LoRA co-training alone.
key_findings.task_dependent_ssm_sensitivity: SSM persistence provides meaningful gains only for document classification, suggesting sequence-level pattern recognition benefits more from adapted state-space dynamics than token-level structured output tasks.
